title: AI in Excel 2: Agent Mode, Plan and verification

questions.question: Which Copilot mode reads and answers but never changes the sheet?

answerOptions.text: Edit (Agent Mode)
answerOptions.rationale: Edit mode changes cells, sheets and formulas.

answerOptions.text: Plan
answerOptions.rationale: Plan proposes steps and, once approved, carries them out and changes the file.

answerOptions.text: Chat
answerOptions.rationale: Chat mode is for questions; nothing on the sheet changes.

answerOptions.text: Advanced analysis
answerOptions.rationale: Advanced analysis adds new sheets with Python cells.

questions.question: Why should you avoid asking a simple question like "Which department spends most?" in Edit mode?

answerOptions.text: Copilot may change your sheet to answer it, for example by adding a helper column
answerOptions.rationale: Edit mode is allowed to change the workbook, so questions belong in Chat.

answerOptions.text: Edit mode cannot read numbers
answerOptions.rationale: Edit mode reads the data; the risk is that it also changes it.

answerOptions.text: Edit mode only works on Windows
answerOptions.rationale: Edit mode works on Excel for Mac too.

answerOptions.text: Questions in Edit mode always return an error
answerOptions.rationale: It usually answers, but may also edit the sheet.

questions.question: A long multi-step Copilot build gives clumsy formulas. What does the lesson suggest trying?

answerOptions.text: Switch to Chat mode and ask it to build the same thing
answerOptions.rationale: Chat mode does not change the sheet, so it cannot build it.

answerOptions.text: Turn off AutoSave so Copilot works offline
answerOptions.rationale: Copilot needs the file on OneDrive with AutoSave on.

answerOptions.text: Accept it, because the model cannot be changed
answerOptions.rationale: There is a model picker at the bottom of the Copilot pane.

answerOptions.text: Run the same prompt with another model from the model picker and compare
answerOptions.rationale: The picker offers OpenAI and Anthropic models, and results differ on long builds.

questions.question: After Agent Mode builds a dashboard, you add a test row to the SalesData table. One chart does not change. What does that tell you?

answerOptions.text: The test row was typed in the wrong format, so nothing can update
answerOptions.rationale: Other items moved, so the row was read; the chart is the problem.

answerOptions.text: That chart was built from pasted values, so ask Copilot to rebuild it with formulas linked to the table
answerOptions.rationale: Only items built with formulas on the table update when data changes.

answerOptions.text: Charts in Excel for Mac never update automatically
answerOptions.rationale: Charts update when their source formulas change.

answerOptions.text: You need to switch Copilot to Plan mode for charts to update
answerOptions.rationale: Mode choice does not affect whether a finished chart updates.

questions.question: Copilot's plan for a vendor ageing report uses today's date. Why does the lesson change it to the as-of date in L1?

answerOptions.text: Copilot cannot use the TODAY function on a Mac
answerOptions.rationale: TODAY works; the issue is that the report would keep shifting.

answerOptions.text: L1 makes the report run faster
answerOptions.rationale: Speed is not the reason; a stable, controllable date is.

answerOptions.text: With today's date the report would change every day; an as-of date in a cell keeps it fixed and easy to change
answerOptions.rationale: You control the reporting date by editing L1.

answerOptions.text: Plan mode rejects any formula with a date in it
answerOptions.rationale: Plans can use dates; you just choose which one.

questions.question: What happened to the =COPILOT() worksheet function?

answerOptions.text: It was retired on 14 September 2026; its jobs moved to the Copilot pane and Claude in Excel
answerOptions.rationale: It never left preview, and the pane now does classify, extract and summarise jobs.

answerOptions.text: It became available to all Microsoft 365 users in 2026
answerOptions.rationale: It was Insider/Frontier only and was then retired.

answerOptions.text: It was renamed GROUPBY
answerOptions.rationale: GROUPBY is a separate summary function, not a renamed COPILOT.

answerOptions.text: It now works only with a Claude Pro plan
answerOptions.rationale: Claude in Excel is a separate add-in; it does not run =COPILOT().

questions.question: An AI-built total uses =SUM(D2:D20), but the invoices run from row 2 to row 21. Why is this kind of mistake dangerous?

answerOptions.text: It shows #REF! and stops the workbook calculating
answerOptions.rationale: It gives a plain number with no error at all.

answerOptions.text: It double-counts row 20
answerOptions.rationale: It simply leaves out row 21.

answerOptions.text: Excel fixes the range by itself when you save
answerOptions.rationale: Excel does not extend a SUM range by itself.

answerOptions.text: It shows no error, so the total looks normal while it misses the last invoice
answerOptions.rationale: Short ranges never show #REF! or #VALUE!; only a hand check catches them.

questions.question: On Excel for Mac, which shortcut shows every formula in the sheet instead of its value?

answerOptions.text: Command + 1
answerOptions.rationale: Command 1 opens Format Cells.

answerOptions.text: Control + ` (the backtick key above Tab)
answerOptions.rationale: Show Formulas toggles with Control and backtick; press again to hide.

answerOptions.text: Control + Option + C
answerOptions.rationale: That opens the Claude in Excel pane.

answerOptions.text: Command + Option + F5
answerOptions.rationale: That refreshes a PivotTable on Mac.
